messages:
anya: heads up — after the NF4/FP4 canary push to pool-a at 03:12 UTC we see ~12% throughput drop and host RSS spikes on small-batch traffic (seq<64). tok/s down, p90 latency up.

matt: ugh. any promql / graphs? which kernel-selector version rolled?

anya: promql snippets: `sum(rate(tokens_served_total[5m])) by (pool)` shows pool-a down 11%. host_rss_bytes{pool="pool-a"} spiking 18GB->26GB. rollouts service shows rollout_id: r-2026-03-18-0310 -> kernel-selector v2.9.1

sophia: saw similar on pool-b earlier but only on sequences <64 and batch sizes 1-4. points to prefetch/host-copy path triggering on small KV hits.

leo: can you upload a quick flamegraph / perf? also did we change `supports_prefetch` heuristics in the kernel factory recently?

anya: quick perf snapshot (compressed):
```
# sampled stack top
runtime::dispatch_kernel
kernel_factory::choose_best -> mem_copy_host
cuda_memcpy_htod
malloc / gpu staging
```
looks like host-copy hot path increasing allocations during the calibration window.

infra-bot: deploybot: rollout r-2026-03-18-0310 -> pool-a completed (automated canary)

matt: my hunch: kernel-factory change in v2.9.1 added a priority rule preferring "mem-lean" kernels for NF4, but some NF4 kernels don't expose prefetch-friendly path (supports_prefetch=false). The selector then falls back to a mem-lean kernel that still uses host staging for KV, causing thrash for many small requests.

anya: current kernel-selector config snippet we pushed:
```
priority: ["mem-savings","p50_latency"]
filters:
  - qtype == NF4
  - seq_bucket <= 64 -> prefer mem_lean
```
that seq_bucket rule is new.

sophia: repro steps I ran locally:
```
python -m runtime.bench --model redwood/nf4-13b --seq 32 --batch 2 --quant nf4 --kernels all --profile --runs 50
# see host_copy_count metric bump and p50 latency +40ms
```

leo: mitigation options:
- revert selector to v2.9.0 on pool-a (fast),
- add rule: if kv_cache_present and seq<128 then prefer kernels with supports_prefetch==true,
- add CI microbench that covers small-batch KV paths.

anya: rolled back pool-a to v2.9.0 at 03:26 UTC — immediate metrics: tok/s recovered to baseline, host_rss down to ~19GB. confirms selector change is the culprit.

matt: great. next: bisect exact commit in kernel-factory between v2.9.0..v2.9.1. I'll take first pass. also add a quick unit in kernel descriptor: `prefetch_capable: bool` and ensure selector respects it.

sophia: I'll add the bench to CI and create a microtest that fails on host_copy_count > 5 per 1k requests.

leo: I'll add a prom alert: `rate(host_copy_ops[5m]) / rate(tokens_served_total[5m]) > 0.01` -> rollback or page.

anya: notes for postmortem: calibration-only change interacted badly with small-batch KV hot path. action items:
- bisect & fix selector (matt + anya)
- CI microbench (sophia)
- prefetched-capability flag + tests (matt)
- alert for host_copy_ratio (leo)
- schedule a small-batch canary before any future mem-oriented optimizations

matt: assigning tickets. will follow-up with bisect PR and patch to selector logic.

infra-bot: ticket created: INF-4872 "kernel-selector: respect prefetch_capable for small seq KV requests" (assignees: matt, anya)

anya: thanks all — will run a quick follow-up sanity after patch. closing eyes on pool-a during working hours for now.
